jobs.title: Mine Engineer Summer Intern (Bald Mountain, NV, US)
jobs.description:
Bald Mountain is an open-pit mine with a large estimated mineral resource in the largest private mining land package in the U.S. The mine is located in White Pine County, one of the best mining jurisdictions in the world, along the southern extension of the prolific Carlin trend. Bald Mountain and the nearby Round Mountain mine make up Kinross’ Nevada operations. 

Bald Mountain is an important contributor to the economy of northeastern Nevada and maintains a comprehensive environmental strategy including wildlife protection, habitat recovery and education.

Job Summary

Under the direction of the Chief Engineer, this person will learn entry-level engineering tasks with a focus on Geotechnical Engineering and/or Blast Engineering while continuously aligning daily functions to reflect Kinross’ values. Project goals will be identified early, based on skills and interest, to support day to day operations and finish with a project deliverable.

Housing will be provided for the duration of the summer internship.

Essential Functions

Compliance with all company policies and procedures including, but not limited to safety, environmental, confidentiality and code of conduct.  

Meets or exceeds established performance expectations set by management. 

Consistently exercises discretion and judgment in job performance. 

Works without risk or harm to self and others.  

Punctuality and regular attendance required. 

Helps develop other department personnel to perform duties listed above. 

Performs other related functions as assigned by supervisor. 

Qualifications and Skill Requirements

1.  Interest and ability to work on highwall design and as-built wall control parameters and/or blast design and quality control.
2.  Ability to work and learn to operate instrumentation in the field in a variety of weather conditions and return to the office for data analysis and project development.   
3.  Working knowledge and skill with P.C. utilizing word processing, spreadsheet, database, and presentation software.
4.  Possesses good communication and interpersonal skills. 
5.  General understanding of mining operations, as well as limited understanding of milling and maintenance operations. 
6.  Strong verbal, written, analytical and persuasive skills and the ability to interact effectively with all levels of employees and management. 
7.  Ability to work independently and also as a member of the management team. 
8.  Demonstrates strong administrative, organizational and technical writing skills 
9.  Must be 18 years old and presently authorized to work in the United States on a full time basis. 
10.  Requires valid driver’s license. 
11.  Minimum of 2 years towards engineering or related Bachelor’s degree and 0-2 year engineering experience. 
12.  Demonstrated leadership ability and initiative. 
13.  Hard working Team Player. 
14.  Responsible to manage the RMGC Environmental Health and Safety Management system in his/her areas of responsibility.

Health, Safety, and Environmental Requirements

•    Adheres to all safety and environmental considerations.
•    Have a strong commitment to safe working practices. 
•    Wears Personal Protective Equipment at all times while in the production environment. 
•    Is alert and observes, corrects, and reports unsafe conditions. 
•    Follows operating procedures and complies with all regulatory requirements. 

Kinross Competencies

•   Strategic Effectiveness
Developing and communicating rigorous and creative business strategies that drive sustainable value.
•   External Engagement
Understanding and building relationships with external parties that strengthen and sustain competitive advantage.
•   Business Focus
Applying commercial rigor and discipline to all business decisions and customer relationships.
•   Living the Kinross Values
Aligning behavior, decisions, and actions with Kinross values and principles.

US work permit required

jobs.title: Process Control Engineer (Round Mountain, NV, US)
jobs.description:
Round Mountain is an open-pit mine located in Nevada, one of the best mining jurisdictions in the world. The mine uses conventional open-pit mining methods and processes ore by mill and heap leach. Kinross began operating the mine in 2003, and it has since become a continuous improvement leader in the Company’s portfolio. Round Mountain poured its 15 millionth ounce in 2018. Round Mountain and the nearby Bald Mountain mine make up Kinross’ Nevada operations. 

The Round Mountain mine is an important contributor to the Nye County economy and, working with local stakeholders, has helped achieve significant improvements in healthcare and education in the area.

Job Summary

The Process Control Engineer is responsible for developing, maintaining, and optimizing process control systems that support safe, reliable, and efficient mineral processing operations at the Round Mountain Gold Mine. This role focuses on improving plant stability, throughput, recovery, and equipment performance through effective control strategies, automation enhancements, and close collaboration with operations, metallurgy, and maintenance teams.

Qualified candidates may be eligible for both a sign-on bonus and relocation assistance.

Essential Functions

Process Control & Automation
•    Design, implement, maintain, and optimize control strategies for crushing, grinding, classification, leaching, adsorption, detoxification, and ancillary systems as applicable.
•    Configure, troubleshoot, and support plant control systems (e.g., DCS, PLCs, HMI/SCADA) to ensure high system availability and reliability.
•    Develop and tune regulatory, advanced, and model-based control loops to improve process stability and metallurgical performance.
•    Lead and support control system upgrades, logic changes, alarm management, and interface improvements in accordance with site change management procedures.
Operational Support
•    Partner with Operations and Metallurgy to identify process constraints and variability, and implement control solutions that improve throughput, recovery, and reagent efficiency.
•    Provide on-shift and off-shift technical support for control system issues impacting production or safety.
•    Analyze process data and trends to proactively identify opportunities for improvement and risk mitigation.
Maintenance & Reliability Interface
•    Work closely with the Process Maintenance Superintendent and maintenance teams to support instrumentation, control hardware, and network reliability.
•    Support preventative maintenance strategies, control system documentation, and lifecycle management of automation assets.
•    Assist with root cause analysis for process upsets and equipment or control-related failures.
Safety, Compliance & Standards
•    Promote a strong safety culture by ensuring control systems support safe operating limits and critical safeguards.
•    Participate in hazard analyses, management of change (MOC), and operational readiness reviews.
Projects & Continuous Improvement
•    Provide process control expertise for capital projects, plant modifications, and technology trials.
•    Develop functional specifications, FAT/SAT documentation, and commissioning plans for automation-related projects.
•    Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives focused on cost reduction, energy efficiency, and operational excellence.

Qualifications and Skill Requirements

•    Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Metallurgical Engineering, Automation, or a related discipline.
•    5–8 years of experience in process control or automation within mineral processing, mining, or heavy industrial environments.
•    Familiarity with CMMS 
•    Hands-on experience with DCS and/or PLC platforms commonly used in mining operations (e.g., Honeywell, ABB, Emerson, Rockwell).
•    Strong understanding of mineral processing unit operations and their control requirements.
•    Control loop tuning, alarm management, and control system troubleshooting.
•    Process data analysis and visualization tools (e.g., Wonderware, PI System or equivalent historians).
•    Instrumentation fundamentals, including flow, level, pressure, density, and analytical measurements.
•    Familiarity with advanced process control (APC) concepts is preferred.
•    Strong problem-solving and analytical skills.
•    Ability to work effectively across operations, maintenance, and technical disciplines.
•    Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate technical concepts into operational guidance.

Health, Safety, and Environmental Requirements

•    Has a strong commitment to Environmental, health and safety.
•    Wears Personal Protective Equipment at all times while in the production environment.
•    Is alert and observes, corrects, and reports unsafe conditions and behaviors.
•    Follows operating procedures and complies with all regulatory requirements.

Kinross Competencies

•    Strategic Effectiveness
Develops and communicates creative business strategies that drive sustainable value.
•    External Engagement
Understands and builds relationships with external parties that strengthen and sustain competitive advantage.
•    Business Focus
Applies commercial rigor and discipline to all business decisions and relationships.
•    Living the Kinross Values
Aligns behavior, decisions, and actions with Kinross values and principles.

Legislative Requirements

Background Check required

US work permit required

Language Requirements

English

jobs.title: Underground Mine Engineer Intern (Round Mountain, NV, US)
jobs.description:
Round Mountain is an open-pit mine located in Nevada, one of the best mining jurisdictions in the world. The mine uses conventional open-pit mining methods and processes ore by mill and heap leach. Kinross began operating the mine in 2003, and it has since become a continuous improvement leader in the Company’s portfolio. Round Mountain poured its 15 millionth ounce in 2018. Round Mountain and the nearby Bald Mountain mine make up Kinross’ Nevada operations. 

The Round Mountain mine is an important contributor to the Nye County economy and, working with local stakeholders, has helped achieve significant improvements in healthcare and education in the area.

Job Summary

The position is intended to provide a university student studying mining engineering or a related discipline with practical experience in underground mine engineering. The intern will assist the Technical Services team with mine design, ventilation, short- and medium-range mine planning, production support, cycle-time data collection, analysis, and special projects while consistently demonstrating Kinross values.

Essential Functions

1.  Assists mine engineers with underground development and production designs, including layouts for headings, ramps, accesses, stopes, drill patterns, services, and supporting infrastructure under appropriate supervision.
2.  Supports short- and medium-range mine planning by updating designs, quantities, equipment assumptions, activity durations, and schedule inputs using approved planning criteria.
3.  Assists ventilation personnel with underground ventilation surveys, including airflow, pressure, temperature, and environmental data collection, and helps maintain ventilation records and plans.
4.  Collects underground operating-cycle data for drilling, charging, blasting, re-entry, mucking, hauling, ground support, backfilling, and related activities using approved observation and data-capture methods.
5.  Assists with special projects such as haulage studies, equipment productivity reviews, development advance analysis, stope-cycle reviews, infrastructure trade-offs, and ventilation or mine-plan optimization.
6.  Compiles, validates, organizes, and summarizes engineering and operational data using spreadsheets, databases, dashboards, mine-planning software, and other approved systems.
7.  Works collaboratively with mine engineering, ventilation, geology, geotechnical engineering, survey, operations, maintenance, and other site personnel to complete assigned work and communicate findings.
8.  Conducts time-and-motion observations underground and records timestamps, delays, travel distances, equipment interactions, and operating conditions without interfering with production activities.
9.  Assists with comparing actual cycle performance against planning assumptions and prepares clear summaries of variances, recurring delays, and potential improvement opportunities for engineering review.
10.  Updates mine plans, sections, drawings, quantities, presentations, and planning documentation under the direction of qualified engineering personnel.
11.  Participate in underground inspections, planning meetings, pre-shift coordination, workplace examinations, and task-level risk assessments applicable to assigned engineering work.
12.  Compliance with all company policies and procedures including, but not limited to safety, environmental, confidentiality and code of conduct. 
13.  Meets or exceeds established performance expectations set by management.
14.  Consistently exercises discretion and judgment in job performance.
15.  Works without risk or harm to self and others. 
16.  Punctuality and regular attendance required.
17.  Performs other related functions as assigned by supervisor.

Qualifications and Skill Requirements

1.  Must possess a professional attitude toward responsibilities.
2.  Must be able to work with little or no direct supervision and work well with others.
3.  Must be able to work in a safe manner and adhere to RMGC safety standards.
4.   Possesses good communication and interpersonal skills. 
5.  General understanding of mining engineering principles and an interest in underground mine design, scheduling, ventilation, equipment productivity, and production systems.
6.  Working knowledge of computers and common word-processing, spreadsheet, database, and presentation software; exposure to mine-planning, CAD, ventilation-modeling, scheduling, GIS, or data-visualization software is an asset.
7.  Strong verbal, written, analytical and persuasive skills and the ability to interact effectively with all levels of employees and management.
8.  Ability to work independently when appropriate and collaboratively as a member of a multidisciplinary technical and operations team.
9.  Demonstrates strong analytical, organizational, data-management, problem-solving, and technical writing skills.
10.  Currently enrolled in a mining engineering or related bachelor’s degree program, with at least two years of university coursework preferred; 0-2 years of relevant engineering, mining, construction, or industrial experience preferred.
11.  Must be 18 years old and presently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. 
12.  Requires valid driver’s license.

Health, Safety, and Environmental Requirements

•  Adheres to all safety and environmental considerations.
•  Have a strong commitment to safe working practices. 
•  Wears required Personal Protective Equipment at all times in underground, surface production, office, shop, and other designated work areas.
•  Is alert and observes, corrects, and reports unsafe conditions. 
•  Follows operating procedures and comply with all regulatory requirements. 
•  Must be able and willing to work underground and travel through active mine workings in accordance with site access, training, and escort requirements.
•  Must maintain situational awareness around mobile equipment, blasting boundaries, ventilation controls, ground conditions

jobs.title: Business Analyst, Project Controls (Red Lake, ON, CA)
jobs.description:
The Great Bear project is a development-stage asset located in the renowned and prolific Red Lake mining district, and represents one of the most exciting recent gold discoveries globally.  The project has excellent potential to become a top-tier deposit that could support a large, long-life mine complex. Kinross’ comprehensive exploration and development program will aim to support the vision of a quality, high-grade, open-pit mine and a longer-term, sizeable underground mine.

Job Summary

The Business Analyst, Project Controls will support project forecasting and reporting using data analysis, dashboards, and presentation material. The role will assist with cost reviews and forecast updates, analyze project performance and cost trends, and prepare reports and presentations. Reporting to the Cost Control and Contract Administration Manager, the successful candidate will work closely with planning and other departments.

Key Responsibilities and Duties

Develop an understanding of the project scope, budget, and schedule.

Develop ‘superuser’ level knowledge of the project cost control system, provide training, and support to the project team members as required.

Support the Project Control team in the preparation of cost reports, forecasts, accruals, cash flows, and performance metrics.

Analyze project commitments and costs at a work package level, assist in identifying trend variances and risks.

Review contractor cost and progress information.

Develop and maintain Excel based or BI models, dashboards, and tracking tools to improve data analysis and reporting efficiency.

Prepare reports and presentations, and executive briefing materials.

Support ad hoc business analysis activities.

Identify opportunities to improve reporting activities reporting processes, data quality, and analytic tools.

Work in a healthy work environment with full support, cooperation, and commitment to satisfy our operation’s goal of being accident-free.

Support a work environment that is aligned with Kinross’ Safeground principles.

Comply with federal and provincial acts and regulations, and legal requirements.

Adhere to all relevant Great Bear policies and procedures.

Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications and Skill Requirements

Degree or Diploma in Engineering or Business, or equivalent. A minimum of 5 years of project business analysis and/or cost control experience, preferably in capital project environments, during engineering and/or construction phases.

Mining experience is an asset.

Proficiency with MS Office including PowerPoint and Excel.

Ability to analyze, summarize and present complex data for information and decisions.

Strong attention to detail.

Benefits

At Kinross, Great Bear, we are committed to Putting People First by fostering employee growth and development, celebrating achievements, and rewarding team success. Benefits offered for this position include: 

Annual Fitness and Mental Health Reimbursement

Employee Share Purchase Plan, Registered Retirement Savings, and Registered Pension Plans

160 Hours of Paid Vacation

Employee Assistance Program

Employee Recognition Program

Health, Dental, and Vision Insurance

Life, Accidental Death & Dismemberment, and Disability Insurance

Training and Development Opportunities

Relocation assistance may be provided to eligible candidates on a case-by-case basis

Work Conditions

This position will initially be based in Toronto, Ontario, with remote work arrangements potentially available. As the project progresses to Construction, the role will transition to regular rotations in Red Lake, Ontario. The schedule for this position is 5X2.

Compensation and Total Rewards

The base salary for the Business Analyst, Cost Control is $100,000.00 to $120,000.00 + Short Term Incentive, + Group Benefit Coverage. 

The hiring range reflects our targeted compensation framework for the role. The actual offer will be determined through a comprehensive evaluation of each candidate's experience, capabilities, and potential impact, along with consideration of internal equity, team structure, and benchmark market data for similar positions. In addition to base salary, Kinross offers a comprehensive total rewards package designed to support employee well-being, performance, and long-term development. 

Use of AI in Our Hiring Process

We use AI-enabled tools to help sort and review applications based on job-related criteria. All hiring decisions, including who moves forward in the process, are made by a human.

3.  Develop crew skills to levels of maximum efficiency and safety.

jobs.title: Heavy Equipment Mechanic (Elko, NV, US)
jobs.description:
Bald Mountain is an open-pit mine with a large estimated mineral resource in the largest private mining land package in the U.S. The mine is located in White Pine County, one of the best mining jurisdictions in the world, along the southern extension of the prolific Carlin trend. Bald Mountain and the nearby Round Mountain mine make up Kinross’ Nevada operations. 

Bald Mountain is an important contributor to the economy of northeastern Nevada and maintains a comprehensive environmental strategy including wildlife protection, habitat recovery and education.

Job Description

The Heavy Equipment Mechanic is responsible for maintaining and repairing a fleet of mining equipment, ensuring optimal efficiency and safety of all machinery. This role demands advanced expertise in various mechanical systems, including braking, steering, and suspension, as well as proficiency in electronic engine controls and hydraulic systems. The ability to read and interpret hydraulic and

electrical schematics is crucial for effective troubleshooting and maintenance tasks. Proficiency with Cat SIS, Cat ET, and Cummins InSite are helpful.

While this role ideally suits an experienced mechanic, we welcome applicants with strong mechanical aptitude and  willingness to further develop skill sets.

The position requires a strong understanding of mechanical systems and safety practices while ensuring minimal downtime for equipment and compliance with Kinross' safety and operational standards.
Work Schedule

This position follows a rotating 5/4 schedule, alternating between day and night shifts. Flexibility to work weekends, holidays, and overtime as needed is required.

Job Responsibilities

•    Adhere to all MSHA and Bald Mountain safety policies and procedures.

Job Summary

The Superintendent, Open Pit will be responsible for overseeing the safe, efficient, and cost-effective execution of all open pit mining activities, including drilling, blasting, loading, and hauling operations. This position provides leadership and direction to operational teams, ensuring production targets are achieved in alignment with short and long term mine plans, budget, and engineering standards. The Superintendent is accountable for the safety, performance, and development of the open pit team and for managing the area operating budget and resources to meet operational objectives.

Oversee and direct open pit mining operations, ensuring safe, efficient execution of drilling, blasting, loading, and hauling activities to achieve production targets.

Lead and coordinate short to medium term operational plans, ensuring alignment between engineering designs and field execution.

Collaborate with Technical Services to review and implement mine plans and schedules and analyze and address deviations from plans.

Ensure effective coordination between Mining, Maintenance, Processing, and Technical Services teams to meet site objectives.

Oversee drill and blast and haulage activities to ensure plans are executed safely and in accordance with Kinross, Great Bear standards.

Mange the pit operation to ensure production targets are achieved and within expected ore grade targets and use all available tools to drive continuous improvement.

Develop medium to long term forecasting plans (people, equipment) to effectively execute operational targets.

Assist with the preparation of annual budgets and business plans and manage operational costs

Collaborate with Senior Leadership, Technical Services, Maintenance, and other support departments.

Coordinate workforce planning, training, and succession development.

Provide leadership, coaching, and mentorship to supervision and production crews, leading by example and visibly putting health and safety first to build a strong safety culture.

Set performance targets and KPIs and monitor, measure, and manage the performance of the team and direct reports.

Work in a healthy work environment with full support, cooperation, and commitment to satisfy our operation’s goal of being accident-free.

Support a work environment that is aligned with Kinross’ Safeground principles and promote Principles across all work areas.

Comply with federal and provincial acts and regulations, and legal requirements.

Adhere to all relevant Great Bear policies and procedures.

Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications and Skill Requirements

A bachelor’s degree in mining engineering or a related technical discipline (or an equivalent combination of education and experience), with 10+ years of progressive open pit mining experience, including at least 3 years in a superintendent or senior supervisory role.

Demonstrated leadership and team management experience.

High attention to detail with excellent organizational skills.

The base salary for the Superintendent, Open Pit is $175,000.00 to $210,000.00 + Short Term Incentive, + Long Term Incentive, + Group Benefit Coverage.

jobs.description:

Kinross Round Mountain is a leading mining company dedicated to sustainable and safe mining practices. We are committed to innovation and excellence in all our operations. Join our team to contribute to challenging and rewarding projects in a dynamic and supportive environment. Round Mountain is renowned as one of the most geotechnically challenging mines in Nevada.

Our Round Mountain Technical Services team is seeking an experienced Chief Underground Mining Engineer to lead the underground tech services group comprising of mine engineers, planners, surveyors, ventilation engineers, and technical technicians for the Underground Mine at Round Mountain Gold Mine. Reporting to the UG Technical Services Manager, you will ensure that the mine’s long-hope stoping mining method is designed, scheduled, and executed safely and profitably. This role will also act as the primary technical liaison between operations, geology, and management. The underground is currently in its early development stages and now transitioning from exploration development to capital development. This is a great opportunity for a motivated individual to build the foundation for the underground mining engineering group, standards, and procedures that will be used for the life of mine.  

Qualified candidates may be eligible for both a sign-on bonus and relocation assistance.

Essential Functions

• Mine Planning & Design
Develop and oversee short , mid , and long range mine plans for a long hole stoping operation using paste backfill and cemented rockfill. Approve stope designs, drill patterns, sequencing, and ground support strategies. Ensure backfill requirements (strength, timing, curing windows) are integrated into the mine schedule. Optimize stope sequencing to balance geotechnical stability, ventilation constraints, and production targets
• Technical Leadership & Team Management
Lead, mentor, and develop mine engineers, surveyors, and technical staff. Foster a collaborative environment between engineering and operations, emphasizing problem solving and continuous improvement. Set technical standards, review engineering work, and ensure quality control across all engineering deliverables.
• Operational Support
Provide real time technical guidance to underground operations, including drilling, blasting, backfilling, and ground support installation. Troubleshoot stope performance issues (dilution, overbreak, paste delivery, drilling accuracy). Coordinate with maintenance, backfill plant personnel, and production supervisors to ensure alignment with engineering plans
• Safety, Regulatory, and Environmental Compliance
Ensure all engineering designs comply with MSHA regulations and Nevada state mining requirements. Support and reinforce site Health & Safety Management Systems and environmental compliance programs. Lead risk assessments for new stopes, mining methods, or ground conditions.
• Backfill & Geotechnical Integration
Work closely with geotechnical engineers to ensure stope stability, pillar design, and sequencing meet safety and production needs. Oversee paste backfill and CRF design parameters, QA/QC, and scheduling to maintain mine stability and minimize dilution.

• Budgeting & Project Management
Manage engineering department budgets, staffing, and capital project planning. Lead or support underground capital projects (ventilation upgrades, dewatering systems, new development headings, backfill plant improvements). Evaluate and justify new technologies, equipment, or software to improve efficiency.
• Data Management & Reporting
Oversee production reporting, stope reconciliation, and variance analysis. Ensure accurate survey control, mine modeling, and engineering databases. Present engineering updates to senior leadership and contribute to life of mine planning.

jobs.title: Design Technician (Red Lake, ON, CA)
jobs.description:
The Great Bear project is a development-stage asset located in the renowned and prolific Red Lake mining district, and represents one of the most exciting recent gold discoveries globally.  The project has excellent potential to become a top-tier deposit that could support a large, long-life mine complex. Kinross’ comprehensive exploration and development program will aim to support the vision of a quality, high-grade, open-pit mine and a longer-term, sizeable underground mine.

Job Summary

The Design Technician supports the development and execution of the Great Bear Project through advanced use of engineering design software, 3D modelling, and drawing development. The role serves as a key technical resource for developing and maintaining high-quality engineering models and drawings that support project delivery.

Key Responsibilities and Duties

Develop and maintain 2D drawings and 3D models using Navisworks, Revit, and AutoCAD design software.

Prepare sketches and drawings for the Great Bear Project as per GBR Engineering direction to support detailed Engineering and Construction.

Coordinate CAD drawings from consults and vendors.

Consolidate and coordinate design information from multiple sources.

Coordinate multidisciplinary design information and identify clashes, inconsistencies, and constructability concerns within 3D models and drawings.

Use 3D modeling software to perform cut/full reconciliation during construction.

Interpret technical drawings to ensure safety and maintenance clearances are observed.

Update and maintain internal drawing packages throughout the project lifecycle, ensuring accuracy and document control compliance.

Contribute to the accuracy and quality of design deliverables through careful drafting and revisions.

Prepare construction level sketches as required to assist in the sequencing of activities or contractors understanding.

Prepare small fabrication level drawings for small miscellaneous projects.

Ensure all field level drawings follow document control standards.

Work in a healthy work environment with full support, cooperation, and commitment to satisfy our operation’s goal of being accident-free.

Support a work environment that is aligned with Kinross’ Safeground principles.

Comply with federal and provincial acts and regulations, and legal requirements.

Adhere to all relevant Great Bear policies and procedures.

Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications and Skill Requirements

Diploma in mechanical or civil engineering technician/technology is considered an asset.  

5-10 years of experience as a Design Technician, Designer, Drafting Technologist, or Engineering Technologist with advanced proficiency in 2D and 3D design software.

Expert level proficiency in AutoCAD and advanced working knowledge of Civil 3D, Navisworks, Plant 3D, Revit, Bentley MicroStation, and other engineering design and modelling software.

Strength in mechanical, civil and/or structural engineering drafting for site layouts, mechanical equipment layouts, and piping design.

Demonstrated ability to independently develop, modify, coordinate, and troubleshoot complex 2D drawings and 3D models.

Detail oriented with the ability to read construction drawings (civil, architectural, structural, mechanical).

Able to perform in a fast-paced environment with changing priorities.

Organizational skills with respect to document control systems for drawings and projects.

Computer literacy in a Windows 10 environment, using Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook, etc.)

Operational experience in a mining consultant environment is considered an asset.

Benefits

At Kinross, Great Bear, we are committed to Putting People First by fostering employee growth and development, celebrating achievements, and rewarding team success. Benefits offered for this position include: 

Annual Fitness and Mental Health Reimbursement

Employee Share Purchase Plan, Registered Retirement Savings, and Registered Pension Plans

160 Hours of Paid Vacation

Employee Assistance Program

Employee Recognition Program

Health, Dental, and Vision Insurance

Life, Accidental Death & Dismemberment, and Disability Insurance

Training and Development Opportunities

Relocation assistance may be provided to eligible candidates on a case-by-case basis

Work Conditions

This position can be based in Toronto or Red Lake, Ontario. Toronto-based employees will initially work from the Toronto office before transitioning to a regular FIFO rotation to Red Lake. Remote candidates may also be considered, with travel and site presence requirements determined based on business and operational needs. Preference will be given to candidates who are currently based in, or willing to relocate with relocation assistance, to Red Lake.
The schedule for this position is 5X2.

Compensation and Total Rewards

The base salary for the Design Technician is $100,000.00 to $120,000.00 + Short Term Incentive, + Group Benefit Coverage. 

The hiring range reflects our targeted compensation framework for the role. The actual offer will be determined through a comprehensive evaluation of each candidate's experience, capabilities, and potential impact, along with consideration of internal equity, team structure, and benchmark market data for similar positions. In addition to base salary, Kinross offers a comprehensive total rewards package designed to support employee well-being, performance, and long-term development. 

Use of AI in Our Hiring Process

We use AI-enabled tools to help sort and review applications based on job-related criteria. All hiring decisions, including who moves forward in the process, are made by a human.

Existing Vacancy

This job is for an existing vacancy.

jobs.title: Senior Mine Engineer - Long Range (Hybrid) (Elko, NV, US)
jobs.description:
Bald Mountain is an open-pit mine with a large estimated mineral resource in the largest private mining land package in the U.S. The mine is located in White Pine County, one of the best mining jurisdictions in the world, along the southern extension of the prolific Carlin trend. Bald Mountain and the nearby Round Mountain mine make up Kinross’ Nevada operations. 

Bald Mountain is an important contributor to the economy of northeastern Nevada and maintains a comprehensive environmental strategy including wildlife protection, habitat recovery and education.

Job Summary

The Senior Mine Engineer (Long Range) is responsible for developing, maintaining, and optimizing the Life of Mine (LOM) plans and designs for Kinross Nevada open-pit operations. This role ensures long-term strategic plans are economically optimized, safe, and compliant with geotechnical and environmental standards. They work closely with technical services, geology, and site management to maximize shareholder value and operational performance.

Qualified candidates may be eligible for both a sign-on bonus and relocation assistance.

Key Responsibilities

1.    Strategic Mine Planning: Run pit optimizations and support mineral inventory reporting requirements, optimize mine plans, fleet sizing studies, create stack plans, and technical studies focused on asset optimization.
2.    Design And Modelling: Create open pits, waste rock dumps, haul roads and stormwater drainages. Able to check block models using drill data, run statistics and create scripts preferred.
3.    Scheduling and Economic Analysis: Integrates short-term plans into long-term, and life-of-mine plans. Perform excel level economic analysis. Support feasibility studies (NI 43-101) as required.
4.    Reconciliation and Compliance: Analyzes and interprets mine plans to ensure alignment with financial, environmental and operational objectives. Perform reconciliation of actuals vs. planned production, updating plans to reflect reality while maximizing NPV.
5.    Collaboration: Work with short range planners, environmental, exploration, metallurgy, geotech, maintenance, and leadership teams to ensure long term plans are technically sound.
6.    Innovation: Researches information to support decision-making and improve processes, technologies or methodologies.
7.    Safety and Mentorship: Contributes to safety culture, and the development of policies and practices. Must be willing to take on cross-rotation assignments within the Technical Services Group for personal development.

Qualifications and Skill Requirements

1.    B.S. Degree in Mining or related discipline.
2.    5 Years of experience in surface mining preferred.
3.    Comprehensive knowledge of the principles and concepts of open pit mining engineering.  
4.    General understanding of mining operations, as well as limited understanding of milling and maintenance operations.
5.    Working knowledge of computer-aided mine design and familiarity with one or more commercial software packages (MineSight, Deswik, Vulcan, Studio NPVS etc.)
6.    Proficiency in MS Office suite of software (Word, Excel, PowerPoint).
7.    Strong communication skills (written and verbal) including presenting to senior leadership.
8.    Technical writing abilities preferred.
9.    Ability to learn quickly and to function within the physical demand requirements.
10.    Understanding of Kinross’ processes and corporate values is an asset.
11.    Ability to work independently and as a member of the Engineering Team. 
12.    Must be 18 years old and presently authorized to work in the United States on a full time basis. 
13.    Requires valid driver’s license.

Health, Safety, and Environmental Requirements

•    Adheres to all MSHA regulations and Kinross safety and environmental standards. 
•    Have a strong commitment to safe working practices.

The role leads supervisors and maintenance support resources while aligning maintenance systems, people, budgets, and asset plans with Round Mountain Gold’s underground mining objectives.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership
- Develop and execute long-range maintenance strategies aligned with Underground Operations business plans, site objectives, production forecasts, and asset management requirements.

Asset Management & Reliability
- Establish fleet lifecycle, reliability, component replacement, rebuild, and condition-monitoring strategies that improve availability, control cost, and extend asset life.

-  Develop, manage, and monitor annual operating budgets, capital requests, maintenance forecasts, contractor strategies, and financial performance against approved plans.

Organizational Capability
- Build and develop a high-performing underground maintenance organization through workforce planning, succession planning, leadership development, coaching, and technical training strategy.

Underground Growth & Ramp-Up
- Provide leadership for underground startup, fleet integration, maintenance infrastructure, maintenance readiness, systems development, and scalability for future growth.

Cross-Functional Alignment
  - Partner with Mine Operations, Planning, Reliability, Engineering, Supply Chain, Safety, HR, OEMs, contractors, and site leadership to support business priorities.

Governance & KPI Ownership

Strategic Responsibilities

•  Minimum five (5) years of progressive maintenance experience in underground hard-rock mining operations required.
•  Minimum eight (8) years of maintenance leadership experience required.
•  Minimum five (5) years leading maintenance supervisors, planners, reliability personnel, contractors, or equivalent maintenance management teams required.
•  Demonstrated experience developing and executing maintenance strategies for underground mobile mining fleets required.
•  Demonstrated experience managing operating budgets, capital budgets, maintenance cost performance, contractor strategy, and long-range maintenance forecasts required.
•  Proven experience with underground mobile maintenance systems, asset management programs, reliability initiatives, equipment lifecycle management, and maintenance planning processes required.
•  Strong underground hard-rock mining maintenance experience required; surface-only mining experience will not be considered equivalent. 

Peferred: 

•   Associate degree in Heavy Equipment Technology, Diesel Technology, Mechanical Technology, Industrial Maintenance, or related field preferred.
•   Bachelor degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Maintenance Management, Business Management, or related discipline preferred.
•   Underground hard-rock gold mining experience strongly preferred.
•   Experience supporting underground mine startup, expansion, ramp-up, or major operational growth projects preferred.
•   Experience leading

Under supervision of the metallurgist, the metallurgical technician is responsible for carrying out necessary testing for quality control and process improvements for both the mill and heap leach facilities. They are also responsible for providing analytical data and maintaining equipment safely and efficiently for the metallurgical department to ensure desired KPIs are achieved in the plant.  The candidate must possess good communication skills, be self-motivated, organized, and consistently align with Kinross values.

Job Summary

The IT Specialist is a hands‑on, customer‑focused technologist who keeps Bald Mountain’s users productive and our site technology resilient. The IT Specialist will split time between first‑line/second‑line support and have ownership of core systems: Windows servers/Active Directory, IGA (Identity Governance and Administration), Nutanix‑based virtualization and storage, Cisco switching and fiber, point‑to‑point and point‑to‑multipoint wireless links, and Dell client endpoints. The IT Specialist will collaborate with OT and plant teams to support industrial networks and site infrastructure.

1.    Systems analysis techniques and procedures, including consulting with end users, contractors and vendors to determine hardware and software or system functional specifications.
2.    Design, documentation, analysis, testing of computer systems or programs, based on site and department specifications. 
3.    Serve as a primary contact for the North America Service Desk; troubleshoot and resolve incidents/requests for Windows 11, Windows Server 2019 and newer, O365, Teams, Printing, VPN, and core business apps with high first‑time‑fix rates.
4.    Provide one‑on‑one and small‑group end‑user training; write how‑to guides and knowledge base articles.
5.    Administer Windows Server/AD, DNS/DHCP, GPO, and patching; monitor backups and recovery procedures.
6.    Operate Nutanix‑based clusters (compute/storage/virtualization) and site NAS/SAN (Dell/Synology); perform capacity and health checks and coordinate upgrades with vendors.
7.    Maintain and administer campus/industrial Ethernet (Cisco) switching, VLANs, QoS, link aggregation, and optics; ensure fiber plant integrity and documentation.
8.    Support site point‑to‑point and point‑to‑multipoint wireless systems (backhaul and access), including design inputs, LOS checks, and alignment/validation.
9.    Support for Cisco Desk Telephones and Teleconference Systems including Cisco desk telephones and teleconference systems.
10.    Partner with Operational and Support Departments on industrial networks, historian/SCADA connectivity, and change management that protects safety and uptime.
11.    Own device imaging/provisioning for Dell laptops/workstations; manage asset inventory and lifecycle.

jobs.title: Senior Geologist (Fort Knox, AK, US)
jobs.description:
Located approximately 26 miles from the City of Fairbanks, Fort Knox is a centre of excellence for the Company as one of the few cold weather heap leach facilities in the world.

Fort Knox

celebrated its 25-year anniversary

in 2021, and has produced over 8.5 million ounces since it began operation. In 2020, Kinross acquired Manh Choh – a project expected to commence production in 2024 and process ore at Fort Knox.

Fort Knox prioritizes being a strong contributor to the State and local communities, and since 2001, has helped support more than 300 community partners and has contributed more than US$25 million to the Alaska Mental Health Trust.

Job Description

As Senior Mine Geologist, you will lead the ore control program at the Fort Knox open pit mine, overseeing a team of geologists and geological technicians. You will manage the full grade control process, from blasthole sampling and QA/QC through grade control modelling, dig line design and mining accuracy verification, with the goal of maximizing ore recovery and minimizing dilution and ore loss. Working closely with mine engineering, operations and the process plant, you will prepare monthly reconciliation reports and drive continuous improvement in ore control practices. You will also mentor and develop junior geologists and technicians, building technical depth across the team.

The mine is located 25 miles from Fairbanks, Alaska. The work schedule alternates between 4 days on/3 days off and 5 days on/2 days off.

Job Responsibilities

Prepare reconciliation comparisons between reserve models and actual mine production.

Ensure high quality of blasthole samples and ore control releases.

Working closely with the mine department, verify mining accuracy and track mining dilution and loss.

Mentor and develop ore control geology team.

Ensure that geologic information is updated in a timely and accurate manner.

Assist other staff with tasks that involve geologic issues. Regularly work with Planning and Mine Operations staff to ensure efficient mining operations.

Keep current on new developments in geology and other fields that might improve efficiency in handling and interpreting geologic data.

Maintain accurate records and files.

Consistent exercise of discretion and judgment in job performance.

Punctuality and regular attendance are required.

Meet or exceed established performance expectations set by management.

Compliance with all company policies and procedures including, but not limited to, safety, confidentiality, and environmental policies.

Work safely in all areas and identify potential safety hazards and work with management to correct them.

Work without significant risk of harm to self and others.

Carry out duties of Mine Geologist as needed.

Perform other duties as required.

Qualifications and Skill Requirements

Employee must have sufficient education to read and write instructions, perform simple mathematical calculations, and keep records.

Bachelor of Science in geology or related field is required.

Must have a strong commitment to safety in the working environment.

A minimum of four years’ experience as a mine geologist is required.

Must have a strong knowledge of blasthole sampling protocol and assay techniques.

Knowledge of Vulcan, Leapfrog, and AcQuire are strongly preferred but not strictly required.

Must have solid verbal and written communication skills.

Must be a self-starter with the ability to work with others in a team environment.

Ability to function within the qualifications outlined in the attached physical demands sheets.

May work holidays, weekends, and shift work as required.

Possession of a valid driver’s license issued by the state.

Reporting Relationships

This role reports to the Chief Geologist 

Legislative Requirements

US work permit required

Language Requirements

English

Ability and willingness to travel

The intern will gain exposure to underground development, production, grade control, geological data collection, and core or chip logging while consistently demonstrating Kinross values.

2.  Assists with underground mapping and sampling programs, including face, rib, back, muck, channel, and development sampling as assigned.

jobs.title: Senior Tailings Engineer (Fort Knox, AK, US)
jobs.description:
Located approximately 26 miles from the City of Fairbanks, Fort Knox is a centre of excellence for the Company as one of the few cold weather heap leach facilities in the world.

Fort Knox

celebrated its 25-year anniversary

in 2021, and has produced over 8.5 million ounces since it began operation. In 2020, Kinross acquired Manh Choh – a project expected to commence production in 2024 and process ore at Fort Knox.

Fort Knox prioritizes being a strong contributor to the State and local communities, and since 2001, has helped support more than 300 community partners and has contributed more than US$25 million to the Alaska Mental Health Trust.

Job Description

Responsible for providing Tailings Engineering support to the department to ensure that the mine functions effectively and safely with minimal impacts to the business.  Implement and improve Tailings management programs to meet or exceed industry standards.  Responsible for a wide range of functions ranging from very simple to very complex, including, but not limited to: deposition planning, water inventory tracking, reviewing technical reports, coordinating facility inspections, quarterly reporting, development of Trigger Action Response Plans (TARPs).  To be familiar with and understand the principles of the environment policy and also to maintain and support procedures and work practices aimed at preventing accidents or injuries.

Note: This position will be filled with a job title of either Senior Tailings Engineer or Tailings Engineer depending on the applicant’s job experience.

Job Responsibilities

Implementation of the tailings management system for both the Valley Fill and Pit Bottom Tailings Storage Facilities (TSFs).

Develop TSF deposition and water management plans which align with the Life of Mine (LOM) Ore processing plan and includes sufficient detail to ensure executability.

Work in conjunction with the Ore Processing, Water Treatment, and Mine Engineering teams to develop action plans to execute the deposition plan and resolve plan variances.

Interpretation of monitoring data and effective communication of conclusions or results

Verification that data collection and management procedures are being appropriately applied.

Collaborate with the Environmental team on water balance forecasts to ensure compliance with internal guidelines and requirements from regulatory authorities.

Review performance and make recommendations for operational changes to ensure the Valley Fill seepage collection system is effective.

Prepare quarterly reports summarizing facility performance and complete reconciliation tasks to ensure continuity of assumptions used in TSF planning.

Lead Tailings Steering Committee meetings and present KPIs to foster visibility and accountability between departments and senior leadership.

Liaise with the Engineer of Record (EOR) on all projects and review technical documentation from EOR and other consultants.

Lead and/or participate in facility inspections.

Assist with implementation and propose initiatives to optimize existing TSF processes.

Keep current on new developments in the tailings and mine waste management fields that might improve operational performance.

Maintain accurate records and files.

Consistent exercise of discretion and judgment in job performance.

Punctuality and regular attendance is required.

Meet or exceed established performance expectations set by management.

Possession of a valid driver’s license issued by the state.

Fill in for Chief Geotechnical Engineer as needed.

Perform other duties as required.

Qualifications and Skill Requirements

Bachelor’s Degree in either Civil, Mining, Geological Engineering, or related engineering field is required.

Candidates must have mining industry experience working or consulting on the management and operations of tailings storage facilities, prefer a minimum of 8 years’ experience.

Must have current working knowledge of all applicable regulations: Global Industry Standard on Tailings Management (GISTM), ICMM, MAC, CDA, etc.  Experience with Alaska Department of Natural Resources Dam Safety (ADNR-DS) preferred.

Experience with related engineering software (AutoCAD/Civil 3D, ArcGIS, GoldSim, MineSight, Pipeflow etc.) is an asset.

Practical experience with advanced geotechnical monitoring instruments and techniques is preferred.

Must have a thorough working knowledge and skill using a P.C. utilizing word processing, spreadsheet, and presentation programs.

Must be a self-starter with the ability to work with others in a team environment.

Effective decision-making and problem-solving skills.

Effective organizational and time management skills.

Strong verbal, written, analytical and persuasive skills and the ability to interact effectively with all levels of employees and management.

Ability to function within the qualifications outlined in the attached physical demands sheets.

This position reports to the Water Management & Utilities Manager

English

jobs.title: Senior Maintenance Planner (Red Lake, ON, CA)
jobs.description:
The Great Bear project is a development-stage asset located in the renowned and prolific Red Lake mining district, and represents one of the most exciting recent gold discoveries globally.  The project has excellent potential to become a top-tier deposit that could support a large, long-life mine complex. Kinross’ comprehensive exploration and development program will aim to support the vision of a quality, high-grade, open-pit mine and a longer-term, sizeable underground mine.

Job Summary

Reporting to the Mine Maintenance Lead, the Supervisor, Maintenance Planning will be responsible for developing and coordinating maintenance plans and schedules that support safe, reliable, and cost-effective operations at the Kinross, Great Bear Project.

The Supervisor, Maintenance Planning plays an important role in continuous improvement throughout site and provides leadership to planners and maintenance teams.

Key Responsibilities and Duties

Build the CMMS for mine maintenance and align with the Kinross procedures.

Develop and maintain a detailed preventative and corrective maintenance plan for mobile and fixed equipment.

Create long term maintenance forecasts and schedules to align with operational needs,

Ensure all work orders are fully planned and ready to be executed.

Ensure work order management and maintenance tracking is accurate.

Collaborate with other departments when necessary to improve performance and lifecycle performance.

Identify improvement opportunities to reduce downtime and maintenance costs.

Participate in planning meetings for operations to align priorities, schedules and risk mitigation.

Ensure all maintenance plans comply with site safety standards.

Communicate with Supply Chain and vendors to support all maintenance projects, critical spare list, and inventory levels.

Plan, schedule, and coordinate major shutdowns, outages, and turnarounds, including parts, materials, and resource readiness.

Develop maintenance KPIs and performance reports for leadership, and mentor and provide guidance to planners.

Work in a healthy work environment with full support, cooperation, and commitment to satisfy our operation’s goal of being accident-free.

Support a work environment that is aligned with Kinross’ Safeground principles and promote Principles across all work areas.

Comply with federal and provincial acts and regulations, and legal requirements.

Adhere to all relevant Great Bear policies and procedures.

Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications and Skill Requirements

A Degree in Mining or Mechanical Engineering, or a Red Seal trade ticket in a relevant field. An equivalent combination of education and experience will also be considered.

5+ years of maintenance planning experience in mining or heavy industry, including planning for both mobile and fixed equipment; experience mentoring or coordinating planners is an asset.

Solid understanding of surface/underground mining and mining process, and related training requirements. 

Demonstrated experience with a CMMS/EAM system (e.g. SAP, Maximo, Oracle, or JD Edwards).

Capable of learning and adapting to new equipment and software. 

Benefits

At Kinross, Great Bear, we are committed to Putting People First by fostering employee growth and development, celebrating achievements, and rewarding team success. Benefits offered for this position include: 

Annual Fitness and Mental Health Reimbursement 

Employee Share Purchase Plan, Registered Retirement Savings, and Registered Pension Plans

160 hours of Paid Vacation

Employee Assistance Program

Employee Recognition Program (Living our Values Award Program)

Health, Dental, and Vision Insurance

Life, Accidental Death & Dismemberment, and Disability Insurance

Training and Development Opportunities

Relocation assistance may be provided to eligible candidates on a case-by-case basis

Work Conditions

This position is based in Red Lake, Ontario, with one week per month spent in the Toronto office. In this role you will work a 5X2 rotation. 

Local candidates, or those willing to relocate, with relocation assistance, will be given priority for this position. 

Compensation and Total Rewards

The base salary range for the Supervisor, Maintenance Planning is $135,000 to $150,000 + Short Term Incentive Bonus, + Group Benefit Coverage. 

The hiring range reflects our targeted compensation framework for the role. The actual offer will be determined through a comprehensive evaluation of each candidate's experience, capabilities, and potential impact, along with consideration of internal equity, team structure, and benchmark market data for similar positions. 

In addition to base salary, Kinross offers a comprehensive total rewards package designed to support employee well-being, performance, and long-term development. 

Use of AI in Our Hiring Process

We use AI-enabled tools to help sort and review applications based on job-related criteria. All hiring decisions, including who moves forward in the process, are made by a human. 

Existing Vacancy

This job is for an existing vacancy.

jobs.description:

Kinross Round Mountain is a leading mining company dedicated to sustainable and safe mining practices. We are committed to innovation and excellence in all our operations. Join our team to contribute to challenging and rewarding projects in a dynamic and supportive environment. Round Mountain is renowned as one of the most geotechnically challenging mines in Nevada.

Our Round Mountain Technical Services team is seeking a Underground Surveyor Supervisor to lead the Underground Survey group for the Underground Mine at Round Mountain Gold Mine. Reporting to the UG Chief Mine Engineer, you will lead the underground survey department, manage survey standards and quality control, and provide accurate, timely spatial data to engineering, geology, and operations. This role will ensure that all underground workings, long-hole stopes, and infrastructure are surveyed, mapped, and reported to support safe and efficient mining. The underground is currently in its early development stages and now transitioning from exploration development to capital development. This is a great opportunity for a motivated individual to build the foundation for the underground survey group, standards, and procedures that will be used for the life of mine.  

Qualified candidates may be eligible for both a sign-on bonus and relocation assistance.

•  Survey Leadership and Team Management
Lead, train, and develop the underground survey team, ensuring consistent technical performance and adherence to best practices. Assign daily and weekly survey tasks aligned with mine planning and production priorities. Maintain a culture of safety, accuracy, and continuous improvement within the survey group.
•  Underground Surveying and Data Collection
Establish and maintain underground survey control networks, including primary and secondary control points. Perform development surveys, including heading markups, line and grade, and breakthrough checks. Conduct production surveys for long hole stopes, including collaring, toe checks, and cavity monitoring. Capture as built data for development, infrastructure, and backfill operations.

Maintain accurate survey databases, digital models, and spatial records. Deliver timely updates to mine engineering, geology, and operations, including 3D models, maps, and progress reports. Support reconciliation of planned vs. actual development and stope performance on a regular cadence as needed (daily, weekly, monthly)
•  Technology, Equipment, and Quality Control
Oversee maintenance, calibration, and proper use of survey instruments (total stations, scanners, LiDAR, GPS for surface tie ins). Implement QA/QC procedures for all survey data and deliverables. Evaluate and adopt new survey technologies to improve accuracy and efficiency.

•  Safety, Compliance, and Regulatory Requirements

jobs.title: Underground Maintenance Mechanic (Round Mountain, NV, US)
jobs.description:
Round Mountain is an open-pit mine located in Nevada, one of the best mining jurisdictions in the world. The mine uses conventional open-pit mining methods and processes ore by mill and heap leach. Kinross began operating the mine in 2003, and it has since become a continuous improvement leader in the Company’s portfolio. Round Mountain poured its 15 millionth ounce in 2018. Round Mountain and the nearby Bald Mountain mine make up Kinross’ Nevada operations. 

The Round Mountain mine is an important contributor to the Nye County economy and, working with local stakeholders, has helped achieve significant improvements in healthcare and education in the area.

Job Description

Under the direction of the Underground Mobile Maintenance Supervisor, the Underground Mobile Maintenance Technician is responsible for safely inspecting, troubleshooting, servicing, and repairing underground mobile mining equipment in both shop and field environments. This role supports reliable production by maintaining loaders, haul trucks, drills, bolters, shotcrete and support equipment, with a strong focus on safety, equipment availability, diagnostic accuracy, and quality workmanship in a fast-paced underground mining operation. 

Job Responsibilities

Comply with all company policies, procedures, and applicable safety, environmental, and regulatory requirements, including underground mining standards and safe work practices. 

Inspect, troubleshoot, diagnose, and repair underground mobile equipment including loaders, haul trucks, drills, bolters, shotcrete equipment, utility vehicles, and other support equipment. 

Perform planned maintenance, component change-outs, breakdown repairs, and follow-up inspections in both underground field locations and shop settings. 

Troubleshoot hydraulic, electrical, mechanical, pneumatic, powertrain, and braking systems using schematics, manuals, onboard diagnostics, and technical support resources. 

Read and interpret service manuals, blueprints, parts information, and equipment schematics to complete accurate and efficient repairs. 

Complete detailed work orders, service reports, failure documentation, and parts requests with a high level of accuracy and timeliness. 

Maintain high housekeeping standards in work areas, service trucks, and shops to support a safe and efficient underground maintenance environment. 

Work closely with operations, planning, warehouse, and fellow maintenance team members to minimize downtime and support reliable production. 

Demonstrate ownership of assigned equipment, tools, and tasks while consistently meeting performance, attendance, and workmanship expectations. 

Support continuous improvement efforts, share technical knowledge with teammates, and assist in developing less experienced maintenance personnel. 

Perform other related duties as assigned by supervision in support of underground maintenance and production objectives. 

Education and Experience

Qualifications and Education Requirements  

Three (3) or more years of heavy equipment maintenance experience preferred, with underground mobile maintenance experience strongly preferred. 

Strong troubleshooting and repair skills in hydraulic, electrical, mechanical, and powertrain systems on underground mining equipment required. 

Experience maintaining underground equipment such as loaders, haul trucks, jumbos, bolters, drills, shotcrete units, and utility/support equipment preferred. 

Strong background in underground drilling and bolting equipment repair is highly preferred. 

Ability to read and interpret schematics, service manuals, technical bulletins, and parts information required. 

Experience with OEM diagnostic and service software is preferred. 

Diesel technology training, technical certification, or equivalent hands-on experience is preferred. 

Ability to safely operate support equipment including forklifts, skid steers, telehandlers, service trucks, and similar tools/equipment preferred. 

Strong communication, teamwork, and interpersonal skills with the ability to work effectively across maintenance and operations teams required. 

Ability to work independently, prioritize tasks, and perform effectively with limited supervision in a production-driven underground environment required. 

Strong computer skills for work order entry, equipment history review, and maintenance reporting preferred. 

Must have a proven commitment to safety, quality workmanship, and dependable attendance. 

Must be willing and able to work rotating shifts, including days, nights, weekends, holidays, overtime, and callouts as needed to support operations. 

Must be 18 years old and presently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. 

Valid driver’s license required. 

Skills

Must have sufficient mechanical knowledge. 

4-5 years of underground heavy equipment repair experience preferred. 

Strong troubleshooting and failure analysis skills.   

Must be willing to work overtime on short notice. 

Diesel technician diploma is preferred. 

Ability to operate various equipment including forklifts, skid steers, telehandlers and service trucks.   

Possesses good communication and interpersonal skills.  

General understanding of mining operations, as well as limited understanding of milling and maintenance operations. 

Working knowledge and skill with P.C. utilizing word processing, spreadsheet, and presentation software.  

Strong verbal, written, analytical and persuasive skills and the ability to interact effectively with all levels of employees and management. 

Ability to work independently and as a member of the management team.  

Demonstrates strong administrative, organizational and technical writing skills. 

Must be 18 years old and presently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis.  

Requires valid driver’s license. 

Reporting Relationships

Works under the direct supervision of the Underground Mobile Maintenance Supervisor.

¿QUÉ RETO TENDRÁS?

Desarrollar conjuntamente con la supervisión los planes de minado y hacer seguimiento del cumplimiento programado, de acuerdo a los lineamientos y políticas de la organización, con la finalidad de asegurar que se cumplan dentro del plazo de entrega establecido en el ciclo de planeamiento.

Brindar el soporte en la elaboración de los planes semanales y mensuales de minado, perforación, voladura, de cables, de tránsito en mina, y descarga en botaderos, stocks y dique, esto desarrollado conjuntamente con el equipo de planeamiento.

jobs.title: Gerente de Almacenaje y Distribución
jobs.description:
Somos Transber, una empresa líder con más de 40 años de experiencia en el rubro logístico y multimodal, y buscamos a un gerente de operaciones logísticas para liderar nuestra nueva Gerencia de Almacenaje y Distribución. Es una unidad de negocio con P&L propio que reúne la distribución nacional terrestre y fluvial, el transporte de gases y los almacenes de la compañía.
El reto: desarrollar el potencial de la carga nacional terrestre, construir el negocio de transporte fluvial para el sector petrolero en la Amazonía, profesionalizar la operación de almacenes y consolidar el transporte de materiales peligrosos, con altos estándares de seguridad y rentabilidad.
GERENTE DE ALMACENAJE Y DISTRIBUCIÓN:
REQUISITOS:
Formación
Ingeniería Industrial, Logística, Transportes, Administración o afines (titulado).
Maestría o posgrado en Supply Chain, Operaciones o MBA: deseable.
Certificaciones en seguridad y salud (ISO 45001), gestión de calidad (ISO 9001) o BASC: deseable.
Experiencia
10 años o más en logística y transporte; al menos 5 en posiciones de jefatura o gerencia.
Gestión de flota propia y/o tercerizada de transporte terrestre de carga a nivel nacional.
Gestión de almacenes: inventarios, WMS, layout y costos por posición/m².
Responsabilidad sobre un P&L o presupuesto de unidad, con metas de venta y margen.
Clientes del sector hidrocarburos, minería o energía, con sus exigencias de HSE y auditorías.
Muy valorado: transporte fluvial en la Amazonía o multimodal terrestre-fluvial; transporte de materiales peligrosos (GLP, combustibles); participación en licitaciones de petroleras o mineras.
Conocimientos técnicos
Normativa MTC de transporte de carga y de materiales y residuos peligrosos; normativa de transporte acuático (MTC, DICAPI).
Requisitos de OSINERGMIN para el transporte de hidrocarburos y GLP.
Sistemas de gestión HSE; Ley de Seguridad y Salud en el Trabajo (Ley 29783).
Control de gestión: costeo por viaje/ruta, rentabilidad por cliente, indicadores operativos.
ERP, WMS y TMS; GPS y monitoreo de flota.
Inglés intermedio.
FUNCIONES:
Dirigir la unidad y cumplir el presupuesto anual de venta, costos y EBITDA.
Gestionar la operación de flota propia y de terceros en transporte terrestre y fluvial, incluidas soluciones multimodales en la Amazonía.

jobs.title: Commercial & Scientific Analyst/Lead
jobs.description:
About the company

In the coming decades, demand for critical minerals such as copper, lithium, and cobalt will continue to grow. These minerals are needed to build electric infrastructure, vehicles, data centers, and electronics. However, the mining industry is making 10x fewer discoveries per dollar spent on exploration compared to 30 years ago because the easy-to-find, near surface deposits have largely been discovered.

KoBold was founded to be the first AI native mineral exploration, mine development, and technology development company. Our goal is to turn mineral exploration into a repeatable science to discover the minerals the world needs—by integrating artificial intelligence, human intelligence, and new technology. Our multidisciplinary teams of data scientists, engineers, and geologists work together to build data systems, design new sensors, and establish industry-leading workflows to develop and test subsurface predictions on our exploration projects.

Our first discovery, Mingomba, is a high-grade copper deposit in Zambia, found after spending materially less than industry average. We are developing Mingomba with the same technical rigor that we apply to exploration. The Mingomba team brings together mine and processing engineers, geologists, data scientists, software engineers, and community, health & safety, construction, and operations specialists. By combining industry knowledge and cutting edge technology, we are developing Mingomba into a world class project that has safer and more predictable outcomes for ourselves, partners, and communities. It is expected to create thousands of good jobs for generations.

KoBold runs exploration programs in eight countries, all with the potential for another discovery.

KoBold is privately held; investors include institutional asset managers T. Rowe Price and Canada Pension Plan Investments; technology venture capitalists Andreessen Horowitz, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, BOND Capital, Durable Capital, StepStone, and Standard Investments; and strategic natural resources companies BHP and Mitsubishi.

About the position

In this role, you will report to a Lead or Manager within the Commercial Analytics team, and work closely within a remote team of 5 - 7 (across North America and Europe) to structure ambiguous problems, build financial and operational models, and provide recommendations to the C-suite for key decisions.

The work will span a variety of topics and include traditional market analyses such as creating supply/demand forecasts and writing commodity outlook reports, and non-traditional analyses as-needed to advance KoBold’s mission – e.g., operational and financial modeling for KoBold’s exploration programs, build vs. buy decisions for KoBold’s technology, mine economics modeling, and scientific communication materials for external audiences s, to name a few.

This is an ideal role for a recent graduate looking to acquire a wide range of skills very quickly. The learning curve will be steep, and the work will be varied and intellectually demanding.

Responsibilities

The Commercial & Scientific Analyst/Lead will:

Aggregate existing research and/or conduct original research to build forecasts and models related to commodity markets, KoBold operations, mine development, and more

Work with the Commercial Analytics and Financial Planning & Analysis team to answer strategic questions from leadership

Prepare materials for the Board of Directors and investors or partners

Use a first-principles approach in collaboration with various KoBold functions to help make decisions or improve operational efficiency (e.g., cost models for technology, HR, exploration programs, carbon emissions reporting, trade-off/sensitivity analyses)

Conduct analytics for critical workstreams in mine development and exploration

Build and maintain financial models assessing project economics

Support others on the Commercial Analytics team on various analytical assignments

Qualifications

A great candidate will have:

Education in a STEM discipline or economics (physics, chemistry, astronomy/astrophysics, or mathematics is preferred)

At least 1 year of experience in technology, natural resources, finance, or professional services

Experience with Python or other scientific computing language and/or financial modeling

Excitement about working on a wide array of problems

Excellent communication and organizational skills

Regardless of formal training, a strong orientation toward thinking from first principles with respect to science, technology, economics, and business

Work practices and motivation:

Demonstrated ability to quickly absorb and synthesize complex information, with a keen eye for detail and intellectual rigor

Exceptional curiosity and eagerness to learn, with a proactive approach to exploring new concepts and technologies

Excitement about joining a fast-growing early-stage company, comfort with a dynamic work environment, and eagerness to take on a range of responsibilities

Ability to independently prioritize multiple tasks effectively

What to Expect

Joining KoBold means getting the opportunity for hands-on exposure to our exploration projects around the world. All employees are expected to travel to project sites, with a minimum of one week per year. Field-facing and technical roles spend significantly more time in the field.

KoBold Metals is an equal opportunity workplace and an affirmative action employer. We are committed to equal employment opportunities for people of any race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, or veteran status.

This position is full-time, exempt.

The US base salary range for this full-time exempt position is $105,000 - $190,000 + 401K and equity.

This role is a key ingredient to this strategy. As an early Engineering Manager on the Data Systems Engineering team, you will have the opportunity to shape how we build our product and organization to realize this vision. Thoughtfully build and lead a team of high-performing software engineers, hiring and growing diverse individuals on your team

Work with the Head of Data Systems Engineering and interdisciplinary leaders across the company on our strategy to advance both our technical product and organization

Collaborate with cross functional peers (geoscientists and data scientists) across the company, learning about mineral exploration. Coach your team to better partner across the company.

Spend roughly 1/3rd of your time contributing to projects as an individual contributor

Our ideal candidate will have:

8+ years experience building production software systems

3+ years in an engineering leadership role with reports

Experience building robust distributed cloud data systems. Bonus for experience building systems managing large geospatial or geoscientific datasets.

Deep understanding of multiple database and data storage technologies

A track record of taking ownership from definition of the problem and delivering large projects with demonstrated impact in an iterative manner

Skilled at dealing with ambiguity and prioritizing effectively from multiple inputs

Formal education or job exposure to natural sciences

Work practices and motivation:

Intellectual curiosity and eagerness to learn about all aspects of mineral exploration, particularly in the geology domain. Open to working directly with geologists in the field across the world. Enjoys constantly learning such that you are driving insights through using our tools in exploration.

Excitement about joining a fast-growing early-stage company, comfort with a dynamic work environment, and eagerness to take on an evolving range of responsibilities.

Keen not just to build cool technology, but to figure out what technical product to build to best achieve the business objectives of the company.

What to Expect

Joining KoBold means getting the opportunity for hands-on exposure to our exploration projects around the world. All employees are expected to travel to project sites, with a minimum of one week per year. Field-facing and technical roles spend significantly more time in the field.
